TITLE: A Strong Son
SUBTITLE: Raising a Boy Into a Man the World Still Needs
AUTHOR: Uncle Al
CODE_RULES: A man does the hard thing first.
Feelings are real. Letting them run you is not strength.
Respect every person. Fear no honest work.
Your word is your name. Keep both clean.
Protect the weak. Stand up to bullies. Never be either.
Sex is serious. Treat people like they matter.
Lose with grace. Win without humiliating anyone.
Go build something. The world owes you nothing.

DEDICATION: For every father standing in the garage doorway, wondering if he’s doing enough — and for every boy who needed a man to show him how.
NOTE_BEFORE: This book is for fathers of sons between eight and eighteen — the years when a boy is watching you more closely than he’s watching anyone else on earth.
If you’ve read the other books in this series, you know I don’t do therapy language. I don’t do motivational posters. I don’t pretend the culture is neutral on boys.
It isn’t. Schools, screens, and peer groups are teaching your son what manhood means every single day. Some of it is useful. Most of it is garbage dressed up as empowerment.
Your job is not to control every input. Your job is to be the man he measures the rest against — the one whose voice still matters when the noise gets loud.
Read straight through or jump to the chapter that matches where you are tonight. Either way, start with the Son’s Code on the next page. Memorize it. Live it in front of him.
CLOSING_LETTER: You picked up this book because something in you knows the stakes. Your son is not a project. He is a person becoming a man under conditions neither of you chose.
You cannot shield him from every lie the world will tell him about masculinity, work, sex, anger, and worth. You can be the counterweight — steady, honest, and present long after the lecture ends.
He will forget most of what you said. He will not forget what you did when you were tired, disrespected, broke, or afraid. That is the curriculum. You are already teaching it.
Finish the job. Not perfectly. Manfully. The world still needs men who build, protect, tell the truth, and stay when staying is hard.
Your son can become one of them. If you show him how.
